title: A call-site answer that replaces grep lists every call site grep prints, not the first few of `uses`
actual: `grep -rn compute_total aaa` (8 calls) is denied and the 'Complete' answer carries 3 lines. `devkb uses` caps its hits ("showing 5 of 7 hits ... omitted") and the hook takes that capped --json list, then filters by scope after the cap. On this repository `grep -rn changed_since_build scripts` is denied with 3 of 5 lines (L1138 and L1177 missing).
expected: Either the answer holds every line grep would print (no cap, scope applied before any cap) or the search runs untouched / the answer says what was omitted (SPEC-DKB-007 R6: never collapsed, a call site grep prints is never left out).
why_it_matters: The agent is told the search was answered Complete and does not repeat it, so it misses callers when changing a function: the exact failure the guardrail exists to prevent.

title: A plain `grep NAME` is not replaced by an answer that drops the substring matches grep prints
actual: `grep -rn fetch_rows lib` is denied; the answer lists the exact-word uses only. `prefetch_rows` and `stop_fetch_rows` lines that grep prints are hidden. Same on this repo: `grep -rn _unresolved devkb scripts` hides devkb/cpp_resolve.py:333,395,396 (`stop_unresolved`).
expected: The search is replaced only when the graph answer equals grep's lines for the pattern as written (word match, `-w`), otherwise it runs, or the answer is placed beside it.
why_it_matters: A replacement that hides lines grep would print makes the agent conclude there is nothing else; the lines are really there.

title: A search that names a docs or config folder is not replaced by an answer without those folders' lines
actual: `grep -rn handler pkg docs` is denied; docs/guide.md:1, which grep prints, is absent from the 'Complete' answer (the graph has no document text). The document-glob rule only covers --include/glob, not an operand that is a docs folder, nor a whole-repo `grep -rn NAME .`.
expected: Pass through (or answer beside grep) when the searched scope contains non-code files that can match.
why_it_matters: Docs, config and README mentions of a name are what agents search for when renaming; they are silently dropped.

title: A definition search with -A/-B/-C on a function longer than 80 lines is not denied with an answer that has no body
actual: `grep -n "def build_everything" -A30 pkg/big.py` on a 122-line function is denied with `pkg/big.py:1:def ...` and '(Body not shown: ... longer than 80 lines. Span: ... Read the span you need.)'. The 30 lines grep would print are not delivered, and the agent must issue another call. Seen in a real agent search (audit/searches.jsonl line 15 (index 14): `grep -n "def extract" -A30 devkb/build_symbols.py | head -60`).
expected: When the body cannot be shown, let grep run (or deliver at least the requested context lines); never deny with only a location for a search that asked for lines.
why_it_matters: A denied call with no content costs a turn and the guardrail's whole point (fewer calls) is inverted.

title: `grep -B N` on a definition is not denied with an answer that starts at the definition line
actual: `grep -n "def handler" -B3 pkg/mod.py` prints the decorator `@decorator` (line 7) and two lines before it; the denied answer starts at line 8.
expected: The answer includes the requested preceding lines (decorators, comments) or the search runs.
why_it_matters: -B is how agents read decorators/docstring headers above a definition; the replacement silently drops exactly those lines.

title: An answer to a search limited by `| head -N` or Grep `head_limit` is never larger than the limited output
where: scripts/devkb_guardrail.py:1043-1052 (is_trim_stage at :200 discards the limit; head_limit ignored)
actual: `grep -rn handler pkg | head -2` and Grep `{pattern: handler, head_limit: 2}` are each denied with a 5-line answer; the search would print 2 lines.
expected: The answer is cut to N lines (R5: never larger than grep's own output), or the search runs.
why_it_matters: The agent asked for a small sample to save tokens; the hook returns more than asked.

title: A `grep -n "^class " file` is answered with the classes, not the file's whole outline
actual: `grep -n "^class " pkg/mod.py` matches 1 line; the added answer lists 7 symbols (constants, functions, methods). In the replay of audit/searches.jsonl (index 94: `grep -n "^def \|^class " devkb/cpp_symbols.py | sed -n 20,80p`) the outline lists constants and fields that the grep never prints and ignores the `sed` window.
expected: The outline is filtered to the kinds the keyword pattern names (def/function, class) and cut to grep's size (SPEC-DKB-007 R5).
why_it_matters: An answer to a different, larger question: up to 1500 characters added to a one-line result.

title: A search for four or more names is not replaced by an answer for the first three
actual: `grep -rn 'alpha_one\|beta_two\|gamma_three\|delta_four' lib` is denied 'Complete'; the 4th name is silently dropped, so `lib/a.py:13:def delta_four():` is missing.
expected: More than three names: pass through (or answer all of them).
why_it_matters: A silent truncation behind a Complete label; the dropped name's lines never reach the agent.

title: A graph built before a file was renamed does not replace grep
actual: After the build, `git mv pkg/use.py pkg/client.py`; `grep -rn handler pkg` is still denied and the answer leaves out every line from pkg/client.py (graph_stale checks the new path with changed_since_build, which is false for an unmodified renamed file, and never looks at the old path). #182's rule is incomplete for renames.
expected: A rename or delete in the searched scope makes the graph stale: grep runs.
why_it_matters: The stale-graph guarantee of #182 fails exactly where a refactor happens: moved files.

title: The 'Next time ask devkb directly' command is runnable when the file path has a space
actual: For `grep -n '^def ' 'my dir/with space.py'` the line reads `devkb outline my dir/with space.py --project .` (3 arguments). Names and paths are not shell-quoted; `--project .` is also wrong after `cd subdir &&`.
expected: shlex.quote the path and name; resolve the project instead of `.`.
why_it_matters: The suggested command (#267, on by default) is what the agent copies; a broken one costs a failed call.
